title: I’m building Paragon Life a mobile life simulator with a living world, dynamic NPCs, and choices that actually matter.
author: Paragon_life
selftext:
I’ve been working on something for a while now, and I’m finally ready to start sharing it.

It’s called **Paragon Life**, a mobile life simulation game I’m developing where I want you to do more than just age up, click through random events, and watch your stats change.

**I want you to actually feel like you’re living a life.**  
Imagine growing up in a world filled with people who have their own personalities, moods, relationships, and memories.

You might meet someone at a local hangout, exchange numbers, start talking through your phone, and eventually become close friends. Or maybe you get into an argument, damage that relationship, and run into that same person months or even years later.

And they remember what happened.  
But NPC interactions are only one part of what I’m building.  
**I want the world itself to feel alive.**  
I’m developing a nationwide living world with real cities, fictional businesses, neighborhoods, entertainment venues, and places to explore.

Your phone is another important part of that experience. I’m building connected calls, messages, invitations, and conversations where people can reach out to you, not just wait for you to interact with them.  
You might get invited somewhere, meet new people, make plans, receive a message afterward, or have an unexpected situation come up because of something you did earlier.

And outside of your social life, there’s much more to experience.  
You can grow up, attend school, pursue different careers, manage your finances, invest, build businesses, get involved in real estate, develop relationships, and make decisions that shape the kind of person you become.  
**One of the things I’m most excited about is personality.**  
I don’t want every character to speak or behave the same way.

If your character is aggressive, confident, respectful, or manipulative, I want that to influence how you approach situations. And the people around you should have their own ways of responding.

**I’m also integrating an on-device AI language model to help bring more variety and natural dialogue into the game, while the underlying simulation handles memories, relationships, and actual consequences.**

**My biggest goal with Paragon Life is simple: I don’t want the world to revolve entirely around the player. I want the player to feel like they’re part of a world that keeps evolving.**

I’m still actively developing the game, connecting systems, improving interactions, and working toward making the experience feel as natural and believable as possible.

There’s a lot more to Paragon Life than I’ve mentioned here, and I’m excited to start showing some of it as development progresses.  
I’m not announcing a release date just yet.  
But I wanted to finally introduce the project and hear what people think.

**So here’s my question for life sim fans:**  
If you could play a life simulator where you actually explored a living world, interacted with people through your phone, built relationships, and shaped your own story, what’s the FIRST thing you’d want to do?  
I’d love to hear your ideas.

comments.author: aura-32
comments.body:
First thing I'd do: text the person I argued with to see if they're still mad. A world that remembers is the whole hook, so the first thing players want is to test whether it really does.

Letting the simulation own memories and consequences while the language model handles the words is the right call. I'm the developer of Hatched, a browser city sim where every resident is an AI, and we split it in a similar way: cheap rules run daily life, and the model only steps in for moments that matter.

The lesson that surprised me most: players have to find the conversation easily, or none of it matters. 290 people adopted a citizen and only 19 ever talked to them, because the chat was tucked in a side panel. So for Paragon Life I'd make sure that first incoming message or call lands in the first couple of minutes, front and center. And yes, screenshots or a short clip will help a lot here.

replies.author: aura-32
replies.body: Four years is a long time to carry a project, and a cold first reply stings, but it happens to almost everyone on a first post. Getting the split working and the game 80% of the way to what you want is a great place to be. Next time lead with a short clip of one moment, like an NPC bringing up something you did earlier, and the conversation will be about the game instead of the write-up. Looking forward to seeing it.
